title: The Day of the Returned Casserole Dish
skyStory: Eighty-seven percent and beginning, ever so gently, to wane, the moon is still tucked up in Cancer, where it is writing thank-you notes. Cancer remembers every kindness ever done for it, in order, with dates. Tonight it wants things returned to where they belong: borrowed books, odd mittens, warm feelings that went unspoken. It has a list. It is a long list.

reading: Somewhere in your life is a borrowed thing that needs to go home: a dish, a book, a tool, a charger. It has been politely waiting. Today the moon would like it returned, with a tiny note attached that says something kind.

Here is the plot twist: when you return it, they will try to give you something back. A jar of jam, a compliment, a story. The [[Six of Pentacles]] is watching closely. Do not say 'oh, you shouldn't have'. Say 'thank you, I love it' and carry it home like a trophy. Receiving is a sport, and today you are in the league.
joel.mission: Return one borrowed thing today with a three-word note tucked inside it.
joel.omen: A neighbour waving from across the road. A small circle of kindness is about to close.

reading: The Rat keeps a mental list of every favour, every kindness, every time someone lent a hand. Today the moon asks you to read one entry out loud. Find someone who helped you level up this year and tell them, specifically, what difference it made.

Do it in your own storyteller style. Not 'thanks for everything', but 'remember that afternoon in March when you showed me how to do the thing, and I have used it ninety times since'. Specific gratitude is a gift that keeps glowing. Watch their face. That is the best story you will hear all day.
nancy.mission: Send one thank-you message today that includes a specific date, place or detail.
nancy.omen: A kettle coming to the boil the moment someone walks into the room. Good timing is on your side.
nancy.stoneWhy: the bracelet on your left wrist

together.text: Share a gratitude feast: each of you list five tiny things you are thankful for from the past month, the more oddly specific the better. A perfect parking spot counts. A dog that sneezed at you counts. Read them aloud to each other if you can.
